About

Research focus

I'm a master's researcher in the Critical Creative Computing Lab at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taiwan, advised by Prof. Ying-Yu Chen. My work sits at the intersection of critical computing and community-based design, working alongside groups often left out of mainstream technology design — LGBTQ+ individuals, immigrant families, and people negotiating care within the home — to understand how they make sense of, and push back against, the technologies shaping their lives. Recent projects include supporting hermeneutical autonomy for LGBTQ+ people in Taiwan (CHI 2026), studying how families collectively make data with a shared domestic object to mediate care (TAICHI 2026 · Best Paper), and co-designing storytelling chatbots with Southeast Asian immigrant mothers (TAICHI 2025 · Honorable Mention). I'm applying to HCI PhD programs starting in 2027, hoping to extend this work — grounded in qualitative and design-research methods including research-through-design, co-design, and participatory design — toward questions of embodiment, gender, culture, and more-than-human relations in computing.

Current Work

Ongoing projects

Collaborator

Co-designing Storytelling Chatbots with Southeast Asian Immigrant Women

Advisor: Ying-Yu Chen, National Cheng Kung University

Co-design workshops on storytelling chatbots exploring how Southeast Asian immigrant women narrate their life stories within trustless and silencing social environments in Taiwan, followed by field deployment to inform design recommendations. I helped design and facilitate the zine-making toolkit that opened each session.

Co-Lead

Collective Data-Making for Family Care through a Domestic Object

Advisor: Yu-Ting Cheng, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology

Extending prior work (TAICHI 2026, Best Paper) on how families and a shared domestic object collectively make and interpret data to mediate care relationships between members.

▶ Watch a short demo of the sofa in action
Project Lead

Short-Video Entrepreneurship Among Southeast Asian Immigrant Women in Taiwan

Advisor: Ying-Yu Chen, National Cheng Kung University

Digital ethnography and interviews examining how Southeast Asian immigrant women leverage personal assets to build entrepreneurial ventures on short-video platforms, and how they negotiate tensions between platform demands and domestic labor — surfacing design opportunities for platform design.

Experience & Service

Work & community

I care about staying close to the communities I study. Outside of my research, I volunteer directly with immigrant families in Hsinchu and help coordinate Taiwan's HCI community — work that keeps me grounded in the field and reflects how much I value hands-on, relationship-based collaboration.
